subject: readModels Error: More than one match found for parameter: ^\s*Number of observations\s*

messages.author: 053ef9917455d1c2
messages.subject: readModels Error: More than one match found for parameter: ^\s*Number of observations\s*
parts:
Dear Michael,

I have found your MplusAutomation package to be extraordinarily useful and I cannot thank you enough for creating and maintaining this R package.  I have stumbled across an issue that I want to bring to your attention and would like to ask your advice on how to handle.  When reading in several Mplus output files in a directory using the readModels function I get the following error:

Error in extractValue(pattern = "^\\s*Number of observations\\s*", analysisSummarySection,  : 
  More than one match found for parameter: ^\s*Number of observations\s*
  C:/MOTG Simulation - No Mediation - Test18/c13133/motg_xony_nom_c13133_r2.out

When I examine this particular Mplus output file it is evident what the problem is - data sparseness prevents the missing data EM algorithm from converging and this produces a message that includes the text "NUMBER OF OBSERVATIONS".  This is why the string search for "Number of observations" in the readModels function finds more than one match.  Here is the full message at the end of the COVARIANCE COVERAGE OF DATA section of the Mplus output file (immediately preceding "THE MODEL ESTIMATION TERMINATED NORMALLY"):

     THE MISSING DATA EM ALGORITHM FOR THE H1 MODEL
     HAS NOT CONVERGED WITH RESPECT TO THE PARAMETER
     ESTIMATES.  THIS MAY BE DUE TO SPARSE DATA
     LEADING TO A SINGULAR COVARIANCE MATRIX ESTIMATE.
     INCREASE THE NUMBER OF H1 ITERATIONS.

     NOTE THAT THE NUMBER OF H1 PARAMETERS (MEANS, VARIANCES, AND
     COVARIANCES) IS GREATER THAN THE NUMBER OF OBSERVATIONS.
               NUMBER OF H1 PARAMETERS :        135
               NUMBER OF OBSERVATIONS  :        131

I understand why the readModels function is crashing here but am unsure of how to handle this situation so that I can flag the problematic output file and/or move on to the next output file.  This issue came up in a small test run of a large simulation study.  I anticipate that this will happen numerous times in the full run of the simulation study and I need to figure out a way to read in all the Mplus output files without the readModels function crashing.  Any insight you could provide would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks much,
Amanda
